text:
evan: Heads up — embedding + rerank lanes in eu-west showing sustained queue growth for 30m. GPU workers are full, GPU util ~98% and p99 latency is spiking.
maria: saw alerts. What queues are growing? embedding or rerank or both?
evan: primarily embeddings low-priority lane and rerank lowlat lane. Redis backlog on emb-queue is ~2200 items, rerank is ~400. ingress rate hasn't increased much.
lee: I just checked network telemetry — intermittent 1-2% packet loss on the ToR to uplink for the 3 racks that host the eu-west GPU pools. TCP retries make the GPUs look slow to the runtime, causes backlog.
jonah: hmm that explains a lot. Runtime sees tail latency from remote kv fetches => KV cache misses pile up. We have admission control but current thresholds assume <0.5% loss.
maria: can we short-circuit embedding less critical requests to CPU-quantized fallback to relieve GPUs while we investigate ToR?
evan: yes — we have a soft-fallback route: model=embed-ldp-cpu-q -> used for non-SLA tenants. Suggest enabling for eu-west from 1760z for next 1h.
anita: oncall, can you confirm the tenant list allowed for fallback? we don't want enterprise customers to be auto-downgraded.
anita: @maria can you run the safety filter? 
maria: running safety filter now. curl command below to check route whitelist:

```
curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN" \
  "https://api.redwood-internal/v1/routes/fallbacks?region=eu-west" | jq '.allowed_tenants'
```

maria: whitelist doesn't include any enterprise orgs — safe to flip for low-priority lane.
jonah: while we do that, I'm going to tighten admission control for emb low-priority lane: decrease `max_inflight`  from 400 -> 150 and `admit_rate` from 1200req/s -> 600req/s. That should cut GPU demand quickly.
evan: paste the intended config change? want to apply via console so ops can roll back easily.
jonah: config snippet (will push to feature flag):

```
lane: embeddings-lowprio
admission:
  max_inflight: 150
  token_bucket_rate: 600
  bucket_size: 120
  fallback: embed-ldp-cpu-q
  preemptible: true
```

lee: also adding a short-term netem shim to rack-to-uplink to drop 0.1% so we can reproduce locally before doing hardware escalation.
lee: run: `sudo tc qdisc add dev eth0 root netem loss 0.1%` on staging harness
sre-bot: Incident INC-2026-037 created for EU-west GPU saturation (assigned: @anita).
anita: acknowledged. I'm going to scale up the embeddings GPU pool by 2 nodes as an immediate relief while net team troubleshoots.
anita: scaling command: `kubectl -n compute scale --replicas=12 ds/emb-runner-eu-west` (current 10)
evans: small note: scaling will increase cost, fine for now — let's track burn in the incident ticket.
maria: flip fallback flag now. done.
jonah: pushed admission config to canary in eu-west-lowprio at 1767777842.
lee: net team is routing a tech to the datacenter; they suspect a fanout switch issue causing microbursts.
anita: after flips: emb backlog dropped from 2200 -> 600 in ~6m. rerank still higher but p99 dropped from 1.8s -> 900ms.
ev an: great. keep rollback plan: remove fallback and revert admission if things stabilize.
maria: action items: (1) net team to confirm hardware fault and patch (2) infra to run reclamation play to rebalance GPUs across racks (3) product to notify affected low-prio customers if fallback lasted >30m.
anita: assigning follow-ups in INC-2026-037. I'll leave the scale and fallback enabled for 30m and then re-evaluate.
jonah: long term note: need per-lane network SLOs and automated admission that factors in packet loss signals; current system only looks at queue depth and GPU util.
lee: agree. I'll add an exporter for ToR egress packet-drop rate into the lane admission controller so we can proactively shed earlier.
anita: thanks team. closing the Slack thread — continue updates in the incident ticket. :thumbsup:
